text:
Amira: heads up — saw CA remove 2 nodes from gpu-preemptible pool in ap-south-1 during a steady batch job run, apps spiked 504s for ~6m. Anyone else hit this?
Jonas: yep, I noticed higher latency and a bunch of pods stuck Terminating. CA logs blamed 'unneeded' and proceeded.
Maria: did those pods have PVs or PDBs? scale-down should respect PDBs by default.
Amira: some had PVs + a couple had PDBs (db-sidecar). Here's the autoscaler excerpt I grabbed:
```
I0212 08:14:33.451321 1 scale_down.go:312] Scale down candidate: node/gpu-3 reason: unneeded (low utilization)
I0212 08:14:33.451347 1 scale_down.go:320] Node has 2 pods with local storage, 1 pod with PDB violation? ignoring? trying to remove
I0212 08:20:43.452101 1 autoscaler.go:980] Removing node gpu-3 after evaluation. maxNodeProvisionTime=10m
```
Jonas: hmm looks like CA thought it was safe but kubelet was still finishing termination. If termination linger > scale-down-unready-time it can get tricky. Which flags are we running on the CA?
Amira: current flags from deployment: `--expander=least-waste --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m --scale-down-unready-time=20m --max-node-provision-time=10m --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true`
Maria: skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true will prevent nodes with local storage from being removed, but it says some pods had local ephemeral volumes? that might be inconsistent with logs. Also preemptible GPUs sometimes reappear slowly which causes rapid churn.
Kei (ops-bot): FYI: there's a QoS spike alert from the job cluster at 08:12. Linked run: https://ops.redwood/example-run/3589 :warning:
Amira: proposal: increase `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 25m for GPU pools and set `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` so CA can reason with actual pod conditions, and flip expander to `most-pods` for better packing. Thoughts?
Jonas: I like raising unneeded-time for GPU pools (they're expensive and slower to replace). But don't enable removing local-storage nodes lightly — we must ensure safe drain. Maybe keep skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true but add `--max-graceful-termination-sec=600` and `--scale-down-unready-time=30m`. That gives kubelet more time to finish termination.
Maria: also consider `--balance-similar-node-groups` off? our node groups are heterogeneous (gpu-a100 vs gpu-t4) and balance logic sometimes prefers removing a whole ng. If we disable it CA will treat groups independently.
Amira: ok patch I tested in staging: changed flags for gpu pools only via helm values for autoscaler-deploy: 
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=25m
--scale-down-unready-time=30m
--max-graceful-termination-sec=600
--expander=most-pods
--balance-similar-node-groups=false
```
Observed: no scale-down during a 40m batch run, nodes preserved, pods drained cleanly.
Jonas: good. Any side-effects on cost? keeping GPU nodes idling will increase bill but reduces 504s. We should combine with a longer `max-node-provision-time` so scale-up windows are stable. I suggest `--max-node-provision-time=20m` for preemptible pools.
autoscaler-bot: note — remember to annotate node-group with `autoscaler.k8s.io/scale-up-disabled` if you want to prevent scaling for specific groups.
Kei (ops-bot): rolling this to prod for gpu pools now (canary 10% of pools) — will monitor cloud spend and scale events. I'll add a Grafana panel for CA remove events per pool. :thumbsup:
Maria: one more gotcha — daemonsets (nvidia-driver-daemon) can block removal if they report high local usage; check `kubectl get ds -n kube-system` and `kubectl describe node` for ImagePullDir or local storage mounts.
Amira: thanks. Plan: deploy canary flags to gpu-preemptible and gpu-reserved, monitor for 2h, then widen. If we still see pods stuck Terminating I'll capture `kubectl describe pod` and send.
Jonas: also add a script to parse CA decision logs to surface "scale-down vs pods terminating" correlation. Quick grep I used: `grep -E "Scale down candidate|Terminating" autoscaler.log | less`
Amira: updated runbook snippet for ops: 
```
If GPU pool flaps causing app errors:
1) check CA logs for 'unneeded' decisions
2) check pod Terminating durations: `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector=status.phase==Terminating -o wide`
3) if >5m terminations, increase `--scale-down-unready-time` and `--max-graceful-termination-sec`
4) consider setting `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 25m for GPU pools
5) keep an eye on PDBs and local storage pods
```
Kei (ops-bot): canary change deployed at 09:05 UTC. Will notify if any scale-down happens in the next 2h.
Amira: cheers — will follow up with logs if anything odd. :coffee:
